title: [CQ-I06a] JetBrains plan review disconnect release
description:
Objective: make the JetBrains plan review handle a lost daemon connection the same way VS Code already does (moe-vscode PlanReviewPanel.handleConnectionChange; the human confirmed this recovery behaviour on 2026-09-11). A disconnect while an approval is PENDING ends that approval as not confirmed and re-arms the dialog for the SAME rendered revision.

Today PlanReviewDialog.onStatus is a no-op, and that causes two defects:
(a) The approve bytes can die with the socket. The reconnect snapshot then shows AWAITING_APPROVAL at the rendered revision, and the dialog stays PENDING ('approval in flight') until it is closed.
(b) The reconnect snapshot can show WORKING at the rendered revision. JetBrains then reports the approval as done, while VS Code reports it as not confirmed.
CQ-I06 DoD 1 ('Both clients consume identical daemon verdicts') needs one behaviour for both.

Deliverable:
- PlanReviewApprovalState.onConnectionLost(), which releases PENDING with a new CONNECTION_LOST_KEY 'moe.message.planReview.connectionLost' that is listed in allMessageKeys();
- PlanReviewDialog.onStatus(false, ...) calls it, and repaints on the EDT exactly as onError does;
- the MoeBundle.properties text, mirroring VS Code's wording;
- named tests in PlanReviewApprovalStateTest.

Out of scope:
- ERROR-frame codeName plumbing. JetBrains still re-arms on every daemon error. The daemon delivers frames in order, so a PLAN_REVISION_MISMATCH always arrives after the newer-revision frame, which has already latched the dialog.
- VS Code, the daemon, CLIENT_HELLO, and the shared verdict corpus (CQ-I06b).

Verification (run fresh, exit 0 required): cd moe-jetbrains && ./gradlew test. WSL has no JDK, so run the Windows gradlew.bat equivalent under the jetbrains-gradle lease and label it as the Windows equivalent.
definitionOfDone: PlanReviewApprovalState.onConnectionLost() turns PENDING into READY with noticeKey moe.message.planReview.connectionLost and returns true. In AWAITING_RENDER, READY, INVALIDATED, FINISHED and DISPOSED it returns false and changes neither phase nor notice. New PlanReviewApprovalStateTest cases prove both.

After onConnectionLost, a WORKING snapshot at the captured revision ends INVALIDATED with STATUS_CHANGED_KEY and never FINISHED. An AWAITING_APPROVAL snapshot at the captured revision keeps approveEnabled true, and the next onApproveClicked returns Send with the captured revision. Named tests prove both.

PlanReviewDialog.onStatus(connected=false) calls approval.onConnectionLost() and repaints only when it returns true. onStatus(true) changes nothing. The new key is in allMessageKeys() and MoeBundle.properties, and the existing bundle guard test passes.
Fresh `cd moe-jetbrains && ./gradlew test` exits 0 and its output is supplied to complete_task.

implementationPlan.description:
MINIMUM IMPLEMENTATION, three files. Report each in modifiedFiles.

1. moe-jetbrains/src/main/kotlin/com/moe/toolwindow/PlanReviewApprovalState.kt:
   - Add `fun onConnectionLost(): Boolean = releasePending(CONNECTION_LOST_KEY)` next to onSendFailed.
   - Give it a KDoc. A dropped connection leaves a PENDING approval's fate unknown, so it is NOT confirmed. The machine returns to READY for the SAME captured revision. That revision is never replaced and nothing is retried automatically. A later WORKING snapshot latches as status-changed and is never FINISHED, matching the VS Code plan review (PlanReviewPanel.handleConnectionChange).
   - Add `const val CONNECTION_LOST_KEY = "moe.message.planReview.connectionLost"` with the other keys, and append it to allMessageKeys(). releasePending already returns false outside PENDING, so do not add another phase check.
2. moe-jetbrains/src/main/kotlin/com/moe/toolwindow/PlanReviewDialog.kt: replace the no-op `override fun onStatus(connected: Boolean, message: String) {}` with a body that mirrors onError:
   ```
   if (connected || !approval.onConnectionLost()) return
   SwingUtilities.invokeLater {
       if (isDisposed) return@invokeLater
       try { applyApprovalState() } catch (ex: Exception) { log.warn("Failed to apply the lost connection to the plan review", ex) }
   }
   ```
   Error handling: the callback must never throw into the dispatcher, and it is a no-op after disposal. Do not show the daemon's status text: `message` stays unused, because the notice is a fixed bundle key.
3. moe-jetbrains/src/main/resources/messages/MoeBundle.properties: add, next to moe.message.planReview.sendFailed, the line `moe.message.planReview.connectionLost=The connection to the Moe daemon dropped before the approval was confirmed - approve again once it reconnects.` Use ASCII only, with no {0} slot.

Run the focused class again: C1-C6 and the bundle guard must now pass, and the existing PlanReviewApprovalStateTest cases must stay green.

implementationPlan.description:
ADVERSARIAL SELF-REVIEW, once, last. Load adversarial-self-review. Read this diff as an attacker. Check each of these:
- Threads: onStatus arrives through the dispatcher's invokeLater, while onStateUpdate runs on the daemon message thread. Every transition sits under the machine's one lock, and the repaint is EDT-only.
- Ordering: WORKING at the captured revision arrives BEFORE the disconnect. The machine must be FINISHED and stay FINISHED, and the later lost is a no-op.
- Ordering: disconnect, then a late ERROR or a send-failed callback. Both must be no-ops in READY.
- Spurious status(false) frames during startup or a daemon restart ('Starting daemon...', 'Waiting for daemon...'). These must be no-ops unless the machine is PENDING.
- Duplicate disconnects.
- After the lost, a click must still quote the captured revision only, never a newer one.
- No automatic resend.
- No text built from the daemon's status message.
- Rails: JetBrains only (no moe-vscode, daemon or wire edits), no .moe edits, no Git writes, and none of globalRails.forbiddenPatterns.
Then write the Serena memory 'task-task-b20f7a40efbd4f56b457888612cd52a8-handoff' for CQ-I06b. It must record:
- the new API (onConnectionLost and CONNECTION_LOST_KEY);
- the corpus mapping: a 'connection lost' event calls onConnectionLost(), and the verdicts are rearmed = READY with approveEnabled, latched = INVALIDATED, confirmed = FINISHED, pending = PENDING;
- the residual: on an ERROR frame JetBrains re-arms without codeName.

executionContract.intendedBehavior: When the daemon connection drops while a JetBrains plan-review approval is PENDING, the approval is not confirmed. The dialog re-arms for the SAME rendered revision and shows a fixed notice. A reconnect snapshot of AWAITING_APPROVAL at that revision lets the reviewer approve it again. A reconnect snapshot of WORKING latches as status-changed and is never reported as this reviewer's approval. This matches VS Code's PlanReviewPanel.handleConnectionChange.
acceptanceCriteria: onConnectionLost() releases only PENDING. Its return values and the phase/notice outcomes in every phase are pinned by named tests.
Neither reconnect path (AWAITING_APPROVAL or WORKING at the captured revision) can reach FINISHED after a lost connection.
PlanReviewDialog.onStatus releases only when connected=false. A source-pin test guards this, following the file's existing dialogSource pattern.
`cd moe-jetbrains && ./gradlew test` (or its labelled Windows equivalent) exits 0 fresh.
invariants: The captured revision is never reassigned, and the machine never resends automatically.
FINISHED is reachable only from PENDING observing WORKING at the captured revision.
Late callbacks after INVALIDATED, FINISHED or DISPOSED are no-ops.
No moe-vscode, daemon, wire, .moe or Git-write changes.
compatibility: Existing PlanReviewApprovalStateTest cases stay unchanged. Only the bundle guard's key count moves from 11 to 12 for the new key.
Every other MoeStateListener implementer keeps its onStatus behaviour.

planningNotes.approachesConsidered:
- Keep JetBrains as it is and change VS Code to keep pending across a disconnect: rejected. That keeps the JetBrains wedge: a reconnect snapshot at AWAITING_APPROVAL with the same revision stays PENDING forever. It also contradicts the VS Code recovery the human confirmed on 2026-09-11, where a transport failure is not confirmed.
- Release on disconnect, then confirm a later WORKING at the same revision anyway: rejected. A WORKING frame after a release cannot prove this reviewer's approval landed; it could be another approver, or a queued message. VS Code reports it as not confirmed.
- A new Phase value: unnecessary. releasePending already gives exactly PENDING -> READY with a notice, as onSendFailed does.
